study.title: Differences in cortical response to acupressure and electroacupuncture stimuli
study.study_design: Within-subject crossover experiment; healthy subjects received both EA and AP in randomized order with MEG recording
study.randomization: Order of EA and AP runs was randomized across subjects
study.blinding: Participants were prevented from viewing insertion and stimulation procedures through the use of an opaque screen; participants told they would receive 'two different types' of acupuncture
study.population: 16 healthy, right handed subjects between 20-44 years of age
study.inclusion_criteria: Healthy, right-handed subjects between 20-44 years of age; screened for safety and compatibility for MEG and MRI recordings

conditions.scan_context: MEG recorded during 15 minutes of 2 Hz EA stimulation at PC-6
MEG recorded during 15 minutes of 2 Hz AP stimulation at PC-6
No acupuncture intervention; subjects sit quietly; used to reduce residual sensations between acupuncture runs

interventions.stimulation_type: Electrical stimulation delivered via inserted acupuncture needle
interventions.manipulation_exact: Needle insertion and manipulation to elicit deqi sensation, after which electrical current was delivered
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: Yes; needle manipulated to elicit deqi sensation
interventions.electrical_intensity_exact: Set to level at which subjects indicated feeling a 'strong but not painful' sensation; delivered as monophasic rectangular, constant-current pulse (pulse width: 0.2 ms at 2 Hz) using a GRASS stimulator (S88 Dual Output Square Pulse Stimulator, Grass Telefactor, West Warwick, RI)
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: All acupuncture was performed by the same licensed acupuncturist
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Subjects were seated with their head in the dewar and instructed to fixate on a centrally presented '+' sign; subjects wore earplugs throughout the experiment; wore a plastic brace on their forearm to prevent fist clenching and excessive hand movement
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Clinically relevant parameters (2 Hz stimulus rate and > 10 min. duration) to mimic clinical acupuncture intervention procedures; forearm acupoints chosen based on ease of access and MEG bias towards superficial brain activity

interventions.stimulation_type: Mechanical percussive stimulation (non-invasive tapping) using piezo-electric device
interventions.needle_type_exact: Blunt/non-insertive; wooden toothpick positioned at acupoint with guide tube (simulating needle insertion); piezo-electric cantilever beam (Piezo Bender Q-503B, Piezo Systems, Cambridge, MA) for stimulation
interventions.manipulation_exact: AP insertion simulated using wooden toothpick with guide tube (previously validated technique); toothpick manipulated and subjects asked what sensations they felt and if there was any pain; then piezo-stimulator tip lowered over acupoint; stimulation consisted of 2 Hz mechanical pecking
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: Subjects asked what sensations they felt during insertion simulation
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: All acupuncture was performed by the same licensed acupuncturist
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Subjects were seated with their head in the dewar and instructed to fixate on a centrally presented '+' sign; subjects wore earplugs throughout the experiment; wore a plastic brace on their forearm to prevent fist clenching and excessive hand movement
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Clinically relevant parameters (2 Hz stimulus rate and > 10 min. duration) to mimic clinical acupuncture intervention procedures; AP mimics 'acupressure' or blunt non-insertive needle (Teishein needle) tapping; stimulus waveform was a single lobe from a 100 Hz half-sine wave (pulse width 5 ms)

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: Subjects asked what sensations they felt and if there was any pain

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: 306-channel Vectorview MEG system (Elekta Neuromag Oy, Helsinki, Finland) housed in a custom six-layer magnetically shielded room
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 15 minutes per condition plus 10-minute rest runs between conditions
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: MaxFilter (Signal space separation; Elekta Neuromag Oy, Helsinki, Finland); xfit software (Elekta Neuromag Oy, Helsinki, Finland) for dipole fitting; FreeSurfer for cortical surface reconstruction and morphing [Dale et al. 1999; Fischl et al. 1999]
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: xfit (Elekta Neuromag Oy); custom analysis tools generated by TW and MH; National Instruments Labview; continuous wavelet transform using complex Morlet wavelets
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: Average inflated brain surface morphed via spherical atlas (FreeSurfer); individual MRI-based boundary element models
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Trials rejected based on amplitude criteria: peak-to-peak amplitude > 3,000 fT/cm in any channel, or eye blinks > 250 mV in EOG electrode; foam padding used and subjects reminded to avoid slouching and remain still; head position monitored using HPI coils
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: Low-pass filtered at 150 Hz for evoked time-course analysis; acquisition bandwidth 0-400 Hz; 1200 samples/sec digitization rate; continuous raw waveforms wavelet transformed prior to trial separation for TFR to prevent edge artifact contamination
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: Evoked response field (ERF) dipole moment time-courses from S1
S1 dipole source localization (equivalent current dipole)

extraction_notes.note: R value for EA beta ERD linear trend is reported as 0.62 in the text ('R = 0.62 and p = 0.01') but as R = 0.63 in Figure 2b caption ('* R = 0.63; * P = 0.012'). Both values are preserved in the relevant neural result entries.
p-value for EA beta ERD linear trend is reported as p = 0.01 in the text and as P = 0.012 in Figure 2b. Both are noted.

No formal quantitative deqi or sensory rating scale (e.g., MASS, VAS) was administered. Sensory responses were assessed only informally during AP insertion simulation and via intensity matching in EA. No numerical deqi scores are reported.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not formally assessed or reported. No guessed allocation data reported.
Adverse events are not reported anywhere in the paper.

No MNI or Talairach coordinates are reported for any source localization result. Dipole sources are described qualitatively as contralateral SI (roughly area 3b) and visualized on average inflated brain surface in Figure 1a, but numeric x/y/z coordinates are not provided.
No clinical or behavioral outcome measures were administered. This was a neuroimaging-only study in healthy volunteers.

Figure 1c table reports peak amplitudes in units of 'x 1e-9' but the sign convention and polarity for some peaks (e.g., M20 for EA = -1.88, M30 = 5.48, M120 = -1.99) suggest both positive and negative dipole moment components. Exact units and polarity conventions are preserved as extracted from the table.

The paper describes AP as 'acupressure' but the procedure is a piezo-electric mechanical tapping device at 2 Hz, not traditional manual acupressure. The arm_type_coded for AP was labeled 'verum_acupuncture' as the paper presents it as an active acupuncture intervention, though it is non-insertive and mechanically delivered.

The study has a within-subject crossover design with only two conditions (EA and AP), no sham/placebo arm, and no rest/baseline arm used as an imaging comparison condition. The 10-minute rest run was used between acupuncture runs to reduce residual sensations but no neuroimaging data from rest are reported as a comparison.

Figure 1c reports significant decreases for EA: M30 peaks (A-B, B-C, A-C all *) and M50 (A-C only *). For AP: M50 (A-C *) and M120 (A-B and A-C *). The figure caption also states 'Significant decreases (p < 0.01) following 5 minutes of stimulation are marked by a red *. For EA this was the M30 peaks and for AP the 130 ms peak.' There is a slight discrepancy in the M120/M130 labeling between text (130 ms) and table (129.4 ms). Both preserved.

TFR results for alpha, theta, and gamma frequency bands over 15 minutes are stated to have been calculated but are reported as 'results available upon request' and not included in the paper. Only beta ERD over-time analysis is reported.

The gamma ERS is described as 'low gamma (~30-50 Hz)' in the TFR results section but described as 'early ~20-70 ms low-gamma (g) ERS' in Figure 2 caption, with the oval in Figure 2a appearing to span approximately 30-60 Hz. The text also mentions 'early onset, event related synchronization (ERS), within the gamma band at ~70-130 ms' in the abstract, which conflicts with '~20-70 ms' reported in the results/methods section. Both reported descriptions are preserved in the extraction.
Trial registration number is not reported. PMID is not provided in the PDF; DOI is extractable from the header (10.1186/1471-2202-12-73).
